newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIAN GOVT PAPER YIELDS UP ON ROUBLE SHORTAGE.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN GOVT PAPER YIELDS UP ON ROUBLE SHORTAGE.

text.p: A rouble shortage on Monday pushed up government paper yields and the rouble, dealers said.
*Average yield on taxable GKO T-bills rose to 18.81 percent from 18.45 percent on Friday.
*Average yield on taxable floating-rate OFZ bonds rose to 28.94 percent from 28.55 percent.
*Turnover rose to 2.82 trillion roubles from 2.68 trillion roubles.
*Central bank sold 50.00 billion roubles of bonds for the finance ministry.

"Long-term GKO discount Treasury bills prices fell by 0.16-0.18 percentage points from the previous closing, so yields have gone up seriously on the current (quiet) market," Vneshtorgbank dealer Sergei Fyodorov said.
"Now, the resistance and support levels are at 19.0-18.5 percent, and I think we shall not reach the 18.5-percent level soon."
He said the current yield of 19 percent for long-term T-bills could be interesting for foreign investors and forecast possible new inflows of fresh funds from abraod.
On Monday, banks transferred a record low volume of 583 billion roubles for trading as they shifted funds to other securities and credits.
On the foreign exchange market, a rise in the dollar, which started in the morning was killed by client sales, dealers said.
